title: Rice with Squid, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Rice with squid, Puerto Rican style is a traditional Caribbean dish where steamed rice is combined with sautéed squid, tomato sauce, spices, and sometimes vegetables. The dish is aromatic, mildly spicy, and carries a subtle sea‑flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puerto Rican cuisine blends Spanish, African, and Indigenous Taino influences.
Squid is usually cut into rings or strips and cooked quickly to keep it tender.
The recipe traditionally includes an “adobo” blend of garlic, oregano, vinegar, and olive oil.
It is often served with fried plantains or avocado to balance the heat.
While Puerto Rico is known for arroz con gandules, this version uses plain long‑grain rice.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Squid provides high‑quality marine protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafood options, squid is low in fat, making the dish light.

items.title: Source of iodine and selenium
items.content: These minerals support thyroid function and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: B12 and B6 help maintain nervous system health and metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from rice
items.content: Using whole‑grain rice adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to squid, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce and adobo seasoning can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: Squid can accumulate trace amounts of mercury; moderate consumption is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, often accompanied by fried plantains, avocado, or a fresh salad. A squeeze of lime adds bright acidity.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of water or broth to restore moisture.
